messages:
arian: Anyone seeing weird canary drift on session-bound routes? We set canary to 10% but prod metrics show ~25% traffic to canary from us-east :confused:

mika: seeing the same. spike started ~00:12 UTC, coincides with a salt rotation job? :eyes:

josh: can you paste the rollout config you used? wondering if conditional weighting + header fallback is interacting with sticky cookie logic

linh: paste from console (redacted):
```yaml
rollout: 
  type: canary
  default_weight: 90
  conditional_rules:
    - match: header("X-Client-Variant") exists
      weight: 10
  header_fallback: true
  sticky: true
  cookie_ttl_sec: 3600
```

mika: aha — `header_fallback: true` means if header missing we fall back to hash-based split, but our hash salt rotated yesterday. sticky cookies still honor old buckets for existing sessions, new sessions get new hash mapping => imbalance

arian: deploy-bot shows the canary rollout started at 00:10 and the salt rotation finished at 00:11, so overlap possible. canary upweighting happened after rotation though?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated by arian at 2025-11-04T00:10:03Z. Salt rotation job completed at 2025-11-04T00:11:02Z.

josh: telemetry sampling (20% of requests) shows ~14% of requests with header present routing to canary, but hash-derived routing is ~32% to canary. That matches 10% config + sticky mismatch bump

linh: minimal repro: requests without header go to hash path. if cookie exists from before rotation, the cookie -> old-bucket -> assigned non-canary. New hash mapping assigns more new sessions into canary. Combined you get >10% overall.

mika: not sure why header_fallback was enabled on this route. console UX sets it on by default when users configure partial header rules. We should change default and add a warning about salt rotations and stickiness

arian: short-term mitigation: disable header_fallback for the route and roll back canary to 0 until we reconcile buckets. Longer: add a server-side guard that prevents salt rotation during active rollouts with sticky sessions

josh: agree. also add telemetry flag to correlate bucket assignment distribution vs header-based assignment so we catch this before customer-visible drift

linh: I'll open a tiny PR to: 1) treat header_fallback as opt-in in console (UX copy + toggle), 2) when rollouts are active block salt rotation cron or mark a hold state, 3) add an admin endpoint to remap old cookies to new salt mapping during controlled migration

arian: thanks. can someone add a short incident note for ops? include exact timestamps so SRE can audit. cc @mika for the console copy change

mika: will do. filing ops note now and adding a console tooltip change to the backlog. :white_check_mark:
